To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the MVTec AD dataset is a comprehensive and realistic anomaly detection benchmark for computer vision, (2) state of the art anomaly detection methods perform poorly on this dataset, (3) the dataset is suitable for evaluating new anomaly detection methods.
the MVTec AD dataset is the first of its kind and the current state of the arts approaches are still far from being able to handle the complexity and diversity of real world data.

(1) the MVTec AD dataset is a comprehensive, multi object and multi defect, high resolution color image dataset for unsupervised, pixel accurate anomaly detection, (2) the dataset is the first to provide pixel accurate ground truth for anomalies and (3) the benchmark indicates that there exists considerable room for improvement in unsupervised anomaly localization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How to create a large scale dataset for unsupervised defect detection?

the following contributions: (i) a comprehensive, multi object multi defect dataset for unsupervised image based anomaly detection; (ii) a thorough evaluation of state of the art methods for unsupverised anomaly detection; and (iii) the release of the dataset and code for reproducible results.
the following aspects: We introduce a new dataset for anomaly detection in the field of industrial image processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a need for more and more advanced anomaly detection algorithms.
the MVTec AD dataset is a very useful tool for benchmarking unsupervised anomaly detectors in a realistic and challenging setting.
the MVTec AD dataset is an important benchmark to evaluate the current state of the field and to drive future research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a new dataset, evaluate state of the art approaches, provide pixel accurate ground truth, and show that there is still room for improvement.
the dataset and evaluation are available at: http://www.mvtec.com/company/research/datasets/anomaly-detection/
we present the first comprehensive, real world, multi object, texture, and defect dataset, that is suitable for unsupervised learning, and provide a benchmark evaluation of state of the art methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a clear need for a dataset that is specifically tailored towards unsupervised anomaly segmentation in natural images.
the development and evaluation of new unsupervised anomaly detectors for natural image data is an open problem and requires a dedicated dataset with pixel precise ground truth.
the development of novel anomaly detection methods is a challenging task and that a comprehensive dataset is needed to evaluate and compare different approaches in a fair and meaningful way.
